interactions.summary: Forese explains that Nella’s prayers sped his ascent, then prophesies the shamelessness and punishment of Florentine women before Dante identifies Virgil and Statius to him.
Jiang stops to underscore that Nella’s daily prayers can lift a soul rapidly through purgatory and uses that mechanism to explain why some infants appear in paradise.

claims.claim: Forese says his widow Nella accelerated his release and ascent through abundant devout prayer.
Jiang generalizes from Forese that the prayers of a particularly virtuous loved one can materially change the speed of a soul’s purification.
Jiang extends the same logic to explain why some infants can appear in paradise: parental virtue and constant prayer may carry them upward.
Forese’s speech also contains a moral prophecy against Florentine immodesty, presenting future punishment as already legible from purgatorial foresight.

signature_moments.moment: Purgatory’s clock is altered by tears: Nella’s prayers make Forese drink the wormwood of torment sooner and rise faster.
signature_moments.source_phrase: with her abundant tears, has guided me
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang’s strongest packet on prayer as a real causal force in the afterlife economy.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns Nella into the model of a beloved whose virtue can carry someone else upward.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It expands the poem’s metaphysics into a broader theory of relational salvation pressure.

chronology_notes.note: This packet preserves a June 26 statement of Jiang’s intercessory-prayer model, one of the source’s strongest causal mechanisms.
